lastPrompt: THE OBSERVATION The network sees a 10 x 10 grid. Rows are numbered 0 (top) to 9 (bottom) and columns 0 (left) to 9 (right). The outer ring of cells (row 0, row 9, column 0 and column 9) is a wall bord…

content.text:
**Observations:**
- **Layout.** Row 0 (inputs 0-49) and the border cells have small first-layer weights, which fits cells that are always wall with no other content. The large weights start at input 55, the agent channel of cell (1,1), the first playable cell. Interior cells have large weights, so the network reads the playable area.
- **Channel 3 (obstacles) is unused in the interior.** Every fifth row (channel 3 of each cell) stays near initialisation scale, while the other channels reach several units. For cell (1,1), channel 3 is `-0.039 0.023 -0.059 -0.040 0.100 ... -0.192`, but channel 0 is `1.703 ... 6.706 ...` and channel 2 is `-1.868 -0.189 -0.338 ...`. The same holds for cell (1,2): channel 3 is `-0.027 -0.088 -0.019 0.116 ...`. Only the border ever has channel 3 set, so the game probably has no interior obstacles.
- **Channels 0, 1, 2 and 4 are all strongly used.** Cell (1,1) has channel 1 `-1.167 -0.135 0.056 -0.415 ... 1.306 -2.250 ...` and channel 4 `1.026 -0.114 -0.006 -0.204 2.015 ... 0.757 -2.062 ...`. Channel 4 (previous frame) has weights comparable to channels 0 and 1, which suggests the motion of the moving objects matters.
- **Output biases** are `[-0.853, 0.091, 0.212, 0.068, 0.382]` for `[no-op, up, down, left, right]`. No-op is strongly disfavoured, and right and down are mildly favoured. These offsets are small compared with the input-driven terms, so they say little about the game.
- I could not reliably trace the W2 and W3 paths by hand, so the output layer is only partly interpreted. The line counting that locates input 55 was done by hand and may be off by a line or two. The every-fifth-row pattern in channel 3 does not depend on that count.

**Reasoning:**
- **Ruled out: mazes or interior-wall games** (Pac-Man mazes, Bomberman, Sokoban). These would need interior obstacle weights, and channel 3 is unused.
- **Ruled out: left/right-only games** (Breakout, Space Invaders, Pong). The network uses up and down.
- **Weakened: Snake.** The agent channel is described as "cells the player controls", which fits a body, and food could be the reward channel. But Snake has no moving objects, and channel 1 has large weights.
- **Best fit: a crossing or collection game in an open arena.** Moving objects (channel 1) are large and time-sensitive (channel 4), reward targets (channel 2) are used, the only static barrier is the border, and the agent moves in four directions. This matches Frogger-style play (moving hazards, goal or collectible cells) better than Pac-Man, which needs a maze. Freeway fits the moving-hazard part but has no interior reward targets and only up and down moves.

**Game:** Most likely a Frogger-like game: an open 8x8 field with moving hazards that end the episode on contact, reward targets to reach or collect, and only the border as a static barrier. It could also be an open-field Pac-Man or chaser variant with no maze. I cannot pin down the exact title.

**Description:** The agent moves one cell per step (or stays put, which the network disfavours) across an open field, avoiding moving objects that end the episode on contact. It receives reward for reaching or collecting reward targets, and the outer wall is the only fixed barrier.

**Confidence:** 20%
